**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 21 already matches our preferred limitation-of-liability position:

- **§21.1** — mutual cap at the *greater of* 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000, expressly stated to be mutual and form-of-action agnostic. "Fees" (§1.5) covers subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap base is meaningful rather than illusory.
- **§21.2** — mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, with data restoration, replacement services, required notices and incident response preserved as *direct* damages (a customer-favourable carve-in).
- **§21.3** — "Excluded Claims" (uncapped) cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is expressly not "damages".
- **§21.4** — savings language preserving non-limitable liability and independence of each cap/exclusion on failure of an exclusive remedy.

I also checked for caps hidden outside Section 21 (warranty §19.4–19.5, insurance §18): §19.4 expressly states the repair/refund remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security or indemnified claims, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or concealed cap exists.

One adjacent note for the deal team (outside this rule's scope): the agreement has no standalone indemnity section, so the "indemnification obligations" carve-out in §21.3 has limited work to do until an indemnity clause is added — that should be picked up under the indemnity rule.
